svg.title: Protest Surge Funnel to the 180-Day Clock
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-02-protest-surge-funnel; chapter number: 6; title: Protest Surge Funnel to the 180-Day Clock; subtitle: CBP protest volumes narrowing to the filing window that governs every challenge; caption: Protest filings rose from about 28,000 a year to 93,000 in 2020. That surge is why CBP's protest team pushes for grouped, well-documented protests filed inside 180 days of liquidation.; assumptions note: The first four stages are protest counts and the last stage is a deadline in days. The figures were reported separately and are not a conversion series. Counts for 2019 and the years before it are approximate, as the speakers gave them.; note: Sources are the U.S. Customs and Border Protection protest team for the volumes and FDAImports.com, LLC for the 180-day protest window.; chart type: funnel; stages: label: Open or suspended protests; value: 106505; display: 106,505; conversion: Backlog as of Dec 1, 2020; detail: Open or suspended protests in CBP's queue when the team reported its numbers.; label: Protests filed in 2020; value: 93000; display: 93,000; conversion: Part of the 221 percent increase CBP reported; detail: Lead entry goes first in ACE, with 10-digit HTS plus Chapter 99 numbers.; label: Protests filed in 2019; value: 60000; display: Nearly 60,000; conversion: First year of the surge; detail: CBP's stated best practice is to group entries that have similar exclusions.; label: Annual protests before 2019; value: 28000; display: About 28,000 per year; conversion: Pre-surge baseline; detail: A further-review request needs a specific because statement.; label: Protest window after liquidation; value: 180; display: 180 days; conversion: After this, the CBP decision is final; detail: After that come 30 days to deemed denial under accelerated disposition, payment of all duties and interest, and a CIT summons within 180 days.

text.title: Protest Surge Funnel to the 180-Day Clock

circle.title: label: Open or suspended protests; value: 106505; display: 106,505; conversion: Backlog as of Dec 1, 2020; detail: Open or suspended protests in CBP's queue when the team reported its numbers.

label: Protests filed in 2020; value: 93000; display: 93,000; conversion: Part of the 221 percent increase CBP reported; detail: Lead entry goes first in ACE, with 10-digit HTS plus Chapter 99 numbers.
label: Protests filed in 2019; value: 60000; display: Nearly 60,000; conversion: First year of the surge; detail: CBP's stated best practice is to group entries that have similar exclusions.
label: Annual protests before 2019; value: 28000; display: About 28,000 per year; conversion: Pre-surge baseline; detail: A further-review request needs a specific because statement.

label: Protest window after liquidation; value: 180; display: 180 days; conversion: After this, the CBP decision is final; detail: After that come 30 days to deemed denial under accelerated disposition, payment of all duties and interest, and a CIT summons within 180 days.

text.title: Assumptions: The first four stages are protest counts and the last stage is a deadline in days. The figures were reported separately and are not a conversion series. Counts for 2019 and the years before it are approximate, as the speakers gave them.
